phase_1.focus: VDiff bridge items + Evaluate seed items. Sections E and F first (worst Bloom's calibration).
phase_1.rationale: VDiff is at 0% — even 74 new VDiff items is only a bridge. Evaluate is at 0% — need to establish the tier. Phase 1 creates the foundation items that prove the content model.

phase_2.focus: Analyze + Difficult bulk creation. All sections in parallel.
phase_2.rationale: These are the largest deficits. Bulk production using established templates from Phase 1.

summary.calibration_note: DL-031 coordinated rebalance (S831 Agent G strategy) addresses ~423 of the 550 Difficult shortfall via Moderate→Difficult upgrades. Combined with 222 new Difficult items, the effective Difficult tier grows from 85 → ~535 (post-recalibration) + ~222 (new) ≈ 757, exceeding the 635 target for the original 2,540 pool. When pool grows to ~3,280, the Difficult target becomes 820 — still within range.
summary.vdiff_reality_check: Even with full recalibration (S831 Agent G projects ~55 VDiff) and 74 new VDiff items, the VDiff tier reaches ~129 — only ~39% of the 328 target for a 3,280-item pool. TRUE VDiff closure requires ~200 ADDITIONAL items beyond this proposal. This is a multi-cycle effort.

impact_projection.methodology: Combines DL-031 coordinated rebalance (S831 Agent G — 600 downgrades + 450 upgrades) with 740 new items at designated tiers.

post_rebalance_only.description: After DL-031 coordinated rebalance (no new items yet)
post_rebalance_only.assessment: Easy is bloated at 40.8% (target 15%) — this is the cost of DL-031 downgrades without offsetting. Moderate is close to target (32.5% vs 30%). Difficult improves from 3.3% → 9.3% but still well below 25% target. VDiff remains at 0%. The rebalance trades Moderate excess for Difficult improvement but creates an Easy surplus that new content must dilute.

post_expansion.description: After rebalance + 740 new items (3,280 total pool)

Easy_1.assessment: OVER — Easy surplus persists because no new Easy items are created. Pool dilution reduces pct from 40.8% → 31.6% but still well above 15% target. Mitigation: strict 'no new Easy items' policy + stop adding definitional items. Additional 283 Easy-labeled items from DL-031 complete the picture. Future: consider Easy→Mod-Easy upgrades for borderline items.

ModerateEasy_2.assessment: SLIGHTLY UNDER — acceptable. Most new items are Difficult or higher; Mod-Easy gets diluted.

Moderate_3.count: ~826 existing (some conversion to Diff via recalibration) + some new items at this tier from the 740 (items designed as Difficult may be downgraded to Moderate during QA)
Moderate_3.assessment: SLIGHTLY UNDER — acceptable. The deliberate focus on upper tiers creates a moderate-tier squeeze that is preferable to the current inflation.

Difficult_4.assessment: NEAR TARGET — within 2pp. Excellent improvement from 3.3%.

VeryDifficult_5.assessment: UNDER — largest remaining gap. 129 VDiff vs. 328 target. True closure requires ~200 ADDITIONAL VDiff items beyond this proposal. This is acknowledged as a multi-cycle effort.

Remember.assessment: SLIGHTLY UNDER — acceptable. Remember is the lowest Bloom's tier and the target is a floor, not a ceiling.

Understand.assessment: OVER — Understand surplus persists (pool dilution helps: 50.2% → 38.9%). DL-031 upgrades (stem rewrites) will further convert Understand→Apply. Still above target; unavoidable with current inventory.

Apply.count: ~1,182 (existing) + ~148 (portion of new items at Apply level based on realistic item design)
Apply.assessment: NEAR TARGET — excellent. The existing Apply surplus helps offset the Analyze/Evaluate under-representation.

Analyze.assessment: UNDER — improved from 0.4% to 15.4% but still 10pp below target. Largest remaining Bloom's gap. Future phases must create additional Analyze items.

Evaluate.assessment: UNDER — improved from 0% to 4.5% but well below target. Evaluate is the hardest tier to author (requires professional judgment scenarios). Multi-cycle effort required.

post_expansion.overall_assessment: The 740-item expansion significantly improves difficulty calibration (Difficult from 3.3% → ~23%) and creates the first Evaluate items in the pool's history (0 → 148). Very Difficult, Analyze, and Evaluate remain under target but are trending in the right direction. The Easy and Understand surpluses are structural — they reflect the pool's origin as a template-generated definition bank and cannot be fully eliminated without deleting items (prohibited per Constitution §7).

risk_1.risk: Content quality degradation from volume pressure
risk_1.mitigation: Phase 1 creates templates and establishes quality baselines before bulk production in Phase 2. Every item must pass CAQS §1.6 six-dimension verification at HIGH confidence. Per-batch governance guard (Rule 5: ≤30 items) enforces review pacing.

risk_2.risk: New items introduce DL-008/DL-026 structural defects
risk_2.mitigation: Governance guard Rule 2 (DL-008 BLOCK) and Rule 6 (DL-026 BLOCK) are active. Every batch is scanned pre-commit. Item template must include empty ExplanationWrong[CorrectChoice] by default.

risk_3.risk: Section E already over IMA target (+1.35pp); adding 120 items pushes to 16.3%
risk_3.mitigation: IMA blueprint allows ±3% section-weight tolerance. 16.3% is within tolerance. Section E's Bloom's crisis (77% Understand) justifies disproportionate investment. If strict adherence is required, reduce E target to 80 and redistribute 40 to Sections A/D.

risk_4.risk: New items skew toward easier tiers despite design intent
risk_4.mitigation: Design templates must enforce scenario-based stems, multi-step calculations, and judgment requirements from blueprint stage. Pre-authoring tier check: 'Would a candidate who only memorized the definition get this right?' If yes → redesign. Post-authoring difficulty review before certification.

risk_5.risk: Template-generated items across packs A/C/D create new clone groups (DL-012 recurrence)
risk_5.mitigation: UniqueConceptKey must be assigned per item. Cross-pack stem-similarity scan (Jaccard > 0.70) run after each Phase. Items that share the same template skeleton but differ only by company names are flagged and diversified.

risk_6.risk: Bloom's distribution cannot reach targets without deleting Understand items
risk_6.mitigation: Constitution §7 prohibits deletion. 1,276 Understand items can only be diluted by pool expansion, not removed. The 3,280-item pool dilutes Understand from 50.2% → 38.9%. DL-031 stem upgrades convert some Understand→Apply. Further dilution requires pool growth beyond 3,280. This is a structural constraint, not a failure.

section_priority_order.phase_1_rationale: Section F has the worst Bloom's distribution (85% Understand) — creating even 24 Analyze + 12 Evaluate items establishes a new calibration floor. Section E is second-worst (77% Understand) and has the most items (415) — large impact per item. Section B has the best existing calibration and the most Difficult items (29) — natural proving ground for VDiff templates.
section_priority_order.phase_2_rationale: Section C variance analysis naturally scales to multiple tiers. Section B bulk production after Phase 1 templates are validated. Sections D and A have fewer items overall (375 each) and proportionally large gaps.
section_priority_order.phase_3_rationale: Close remaining gaps. Prioritize sections where Analyze/Evaluate targets are furthest from achieved levels.

recommendation: PROCEED — 740 new items across 6 sections, phased over 3 stages, with emphasis on Analyze/Evaluate/Difficult tiers. Sections E and F are the critical priority in Phase 1 due to catastrophic Bloom's calibration (77% and 85% Understand respectively). Acknowledge that Very Difficult, Analyze, and Evaluate will remain under CAQS targets even after full execution — these are structural gaps that require content creation cycles beyond S833 scope.
